title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Acute Kidney Injury and aHUS
authors_or_organization: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Work Group

excerpts.source_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Acute Kidney Injury and aHUS
excerpts.section_title: Diagnostic Evaluation and Initial Targeted Therapy of Thrombotic Microangiopathies and aHUS
excerpts.key_recommendation: In patients presenting with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury, initiate prompt evaluation for ADAMTS13 activity and complement dysregulation. Prompt initiation of terminal complement C5 inhibition (eculizumab/ravulizumab) is strongly recommended once thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is excluded.

excerpts.source_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Acute Kidney Injury and aHUS
excerpts.section_title: Drug-Associated Acute Kidney Injury and Nephrotoxicity Management
excerpts.key_recommendation: Discontinue potential nephrotoxic and renally cleared metabolic stressors immediately upon recognition of acute kidney injury or severe metabolic decompensation.

title: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2024

excerpts.source_title: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2024
excerpts.section_title: Hospital Care, Secondary Diabetes, and Drug-Induced Severe Hyperglycemia
excerpts.key_recommendation: Patients receiving oncologic chemotherapy (such as capecitabine or checkpoint inhibitors) who develop acute symptomatic hyperglycemia and severe electrolyte derangements (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia) require temporary drug suspension, continuous intravenous insulin titration, and vigorous potassium repletion prior to resumption.

title: AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Management of Stroke and Pseudobulbar Affect 2023
authors_or_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA)

excerpts.source_title: AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Management of Stroke and Pseudobulbar Affect 2023
excerpts.organization_or_publisher: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
excerpts.section_title: Post-Stroke Emotional Incontinence and Pseudobulbar Affect (PBA)
excerpts.key_recommendation: Pseudobulbar affect (PBA) characterized by involuntary, uncontrollable crying or laughing disproportionate to mood after pontine, cerebellar, or hemispheric stroke should be differentiated from post-stroke depression. Treatment with dextromethorphan/quinidine or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) such as citalopram/sertraline is recommended to alleviate affective lability and improve quality of life.

excerpts.source_title: AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Management of Stroke and Pseudobulbar Affect 2023
excerpts.organization_or_publisher: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
excerpts.section_title: Long-term Motor and Cognitive Rehabilitation Following Hemorrhagic Stroke
excerpts.key_recommendation: Long-term motor recovery and spasticity management post-hemorrhagic stroke requires multi-disciplinary physical rehabilitation, blood pressure optimization (target < 130/80 mmHg), neurocognitive training, and structured functional assessment.

title: EULAR/ACR 2023 Recommendations for the Management of Neuropsychiatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
authors_or_organization: European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) & American College of Rheumatology (ACR)

excerpts.source_title: EULAR/ACR 2023 Recommendations for the Management of Neuropsychiatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
excerpts.section_title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Inflammatory and Thrombotic Central NPSLE
excerpts.key_recommendation: In young patients presenting with acute motor/speech deficits, dysarthria, and systemic autoimmune signs, prompt neuroimaging and lumbar puncture are mandatory to rule out central infections and ischemia. For inflammatory NPSLE, aggressive pulsed intravenous methylprednisolone followed by high-potency immunosuppression (intravenous cyclophosphamide or rituximab) combined with hydroxychloroquine is recommended.

title: Endocrine Society / ACOG Guidelines for Hypoparathyroidism in Pregnancy
authors_or_organization: Endocrine Society and American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)

excerpts.source_title: Endocrine Society / ACOG Guidelines for Hypoparathyroidism in Pregnancy
excerpts.section_title: Third Trimester Maternal and Fetal Calcium Regulation in 22q11.2 Microdeletion / Primary Hypoparathyroidism
excerpts.key_recommendation: In pregnant patients with primary hypoparathyroidism (including 22q11.2 deletion syndrome), maintain maternal albumin-corrected calcium in the low-to-normal range (8.5–9.0 mg/dL) using oral calcium carbonate and active vitamin D (calcitriol). Avoid maternal hypercalcemia to prevent fetal parathyroid suppression and neonatal tetany, and closely monitor urinary calcium excretion.

title: AAO Preferred Practice Pattern for Uveal Diseases
authors_or_organization: American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Retina/Intraocular Inflammation Panel

excerpts.source_title: AAO Preferred Practice Pattern for Uveal Diseases
excerpts.section_title: Management of Idiopathic Uveal Effusion Syndrome and Secondary Ocular Hypertension
excerpts.key_recommendation: Uveal effusion syndrome (UES) must be differentiated from angle-closure glaucoma and Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease using B-scan ultrasonography, ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM), and optical coherence tomography (OCT). Primary medical management includes topical hypotensive agents and high-dose systemic/topical corticosteroids, with surgical scleral decompression or sclerectomy reserved for refractory exudative retinal detachment.

title: FIGO 2024 Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Gestational Trophoblastic Disease
authors_or_organization: International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) Gynecologic Oncology Committee
edition: FIGO Staging and Clinical Practice Guidelines 2024

excerpts.source_title: FIGO 2024 Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Gestational Trophoblastic Disease
excerpts.organization_or_publisher: International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO)
excerpts.section_title: Metastatic Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia and Pulmonary Choriocarcinoma
excerpts.key_recommendation: In women with abnormal vaginal bleeding, hemoptysis, and pulmonary nodules following a molar or non-molar pregnancy, elevated quantitative serum beta-hCG confirms the diagnosis of metastatic choriocarcinoma without requiring biopsy, which is contraindicated due to severe bleeding risk. Prompt FIGO/WHO prognostic scoring determines whether single-agent (methotrexate) or multi-agent (EMA-CO) chemotherapy is indicated.
